user_input: My roommate just bagged a 24 LPA offer at a fintech company, and he literally slept through most of the lectures and copied my DSA sheets. I’ve been coding 8 hours a day, maintaining a 9.1 CGPA, and I got rejected in the first round of the same company because of 'cultural fit'. How is this even fair? I feel like my hard work is completely worthless while everyone around me is sailing through with zero effort.

Everyone in my college WhatsApp group is sharing screenshots of their internship offer letters, and I am still stuck with two backlogs and a 6.2 CGPA. My dad called me today and said my cousin just bought a car from his joining bonus, and then he just went silent. I feel like a shadow compared to them, like I'm eating crumbs while they get the whole feast.

I literally had to take an education loan just to pay for my semester fees, and my lab partner just bought a customized gaming laptop without even blinking. He skips class, fails his test cases, and yet he has a referral waiting for him at his uncle's firm. I'm drowning in debt and anxiety, and it feels like the universe decided I don't deserve the same head start no matter how hard I grind.

My entire family keeps talking about my cousin who cleared the UPSC prelims on her first try, while I'm struggling to even get a callback for an entry-level QA role. During dinners, they look at me with this pity that makes me want to scream or just disappear under the table. I'm doing everything right, studying till 3 AM, but compared to her, I'm just the family failure.

All my friends are posting stories from their fancy weekend trips and team dinners at their new tech jobs, while I'm stuck in my PG room eating instant noodles and preparing for another mock test. I feel so left behind, like everyone got the invitation to adulthood and I was left at the gate. Why does everyone else get to move on while I'm frozen in time?

I’ve spent the last 8 months grinding LeetCode, barely sleeping, skipped my sister's wedding to prep for the FAANG drive. Today, this guy from my batch who literally copied my DBMS assignments and barely knows what a pointer is gets an offer for 32 LPA because he got lucky with an easy interviewer. I got rejected in the HR round. Why does it feel like my hard work is actively being mocked by the universe? I feel so empty and cheated.

My roommate's parents bought him an iPad Pro, paid for premium coding bootcamps, and literally call him every day to cheer him up. He just scored a 9.4 CGPA while I'm struggling at 6.8, working a part-time night shift at a local store just to pay for my semester mess bills. We attend the exact same lectures, but his life is set on easy mode while I'm drowning. It makes me hate him sometimes, even though he's a decent guy. I feel so left behind.

My cousin just got placed at an MNC with a massive signing bonus, and now my family's WhatsApp group is flooded with congratulations. Meanwhile, my dad called me today to ask if I've even cleared my active backlogs from 3rd semester. He didn't even ask how my health was. I feel like an absolute ghost in my own family, just a shadow compared to my cousin's shining success. Why is my value tied entirely to how much more he makes than me?

I look at these guys from Tier-1 colleges posting on LinkedIn about their on-campus internship offers from Google and Uber, and then I look at my absolute dumpster fire of a Tier-3 college. We don't even have a functioning placement cell. I am working ten times harder just to get a single resume view, while they get off-campus interviews handed to them on a silver platter just because of a brand name. I feel so bitter and exhausted from fighting a rigged system.

Everyone on my floor is going out for weekend trips, posting stories at cafes, and celebrating their successful mock test scores together. Meanwhile, I'm sitting in this cramped hostel room staring at failed compiler errors in my OS lab, completely broke and isolated. It feels like everyone got a manual on how to balance life, secure a high-paying future, and make friends, while my copy was completely blank. I just feel so deprived of a normal youth.

Everyone in my wing is celebrating. Sharma got 24 LPA at a fintech firm and even the guys who used to copy my DBMS lab codes have bagged 12+ LPA offers. I’m sitting here with my 6 LPA mass recruiter offer, feeling like absolute trash. My dad called today and literally asked why I couldn't crack the product-based companies when we pay the same tuition fees. I feel so hollow. I worked twice as hard as them, didn't sleep for months, and I'm left with crumbs.

The relative grading in our department is a joke. I scored 82 in the end-sems, which would be an A anywhere else, but because the toppers pushed the average to 88, I got a C-grade. My CGPA dropped to 7.1. My roommate didn't even study half as much, got lucky with some MCQ guesses, and has an 8.9. I feel cheated. No matter how much I grind in the library, the system rewards luck and curves my efforts down to nothing.

I’m looking at the LeetCode leaderboard of our college club and I just want to throw my laptop. These sophomore kids are already Knight level, solving hard DFS/BFS problems in minutes, and I am struggling to debug a simple linked list implementation for my DSA lab tomorrow. I spent my whole weekend on this and got nothing but TLE errors. It feels like everyone else has this secret cheat code for coding while I’m lagging miles behind, running on fumes.

My WhatsApp group is flooded with photos of my friends chilling at cafes and planning weekend trips to hills. I couldn't go because I had to cover my backlog in Operating Systems and also manage my part-time tutoring job to pay for my mess bills. They talk about spending 2k on a single dinner like it’s pocket change, while I have to calculate every rupee. I don't hate them, but I hate how easy their lives look compared to this constant survival mode I'm in.

My cousin just got admission into a top Ivy League for MS, and my mom has been on my neck since yesterday. She keeps dropping passive-aggressive hints about how 'some kids' make their parents proud while I am sitting with a backlog in my 5th sem. I’m doing my best just to keep my head above water here, but to them, I am the ultimate failure of the family. I feel so small and empty inside, like no matter what I do, I will always be the disappointment.

Everyone in my DSA lab is flexing their off-campus internship offers on the WhatsApp group. I've been grinding LeetCode till 3 AM every single night, skipped my grandmother's funeral to prep for the mock tests, and I still can't clear a single OA. Meanwhile, this guy who literally copied my operating systems assignments all semester just bagged an 80k/month stipend because his dad had some connection. It makes me sick to my stomach. Why does it feel like my hard work is just being thrown into a black hole while everyone else gets a free pass?

My roommate barely opens his books, literally plays Valorant till dawn, and somehow got an S-grade in the compiler design project because his group did all the heavy lifting. I worked myself to actual physical sickness, skipped meals to debug my code, and got a C-grade because the external examiner was in a bad mood during the viva. My parents called me today asking why I couldn't be more like him. It feels like no matter how much effort I put in, the universe is gatekeeping success from me.

I’m sitting in this crappy tier-3 hostel room looking at my high school friends' LinkedIn posts. They're all at top IITs or NITs, posting about their summer research internships in Europe and getting massive pre-placement offers. I couldn't crack JEE because of my panic attacks, and now I'm paying the price forever. We started at the exact same place, but I'm stuck eating cold mess food trying to self-study obsolete web dev while they get world-class mentorship. I feel like my life is already over before it even started.

Every single relative of mine is in our family WhatsApp group praising my cousin who got a 45 LPA job at Amazon. My mom looked at me with so much quiet disappointment today, then handed me a plate of food without saying a word. I’ve been applying to 50 off-campus roles every single day, tailoring my resume, doing cold emails on LinkedIn, and I don't even get an automated rejection mail. Why does she get to be the golden child while I feel like a massive financial burden who can't even get an unpaid internship?

The placement cell just released the statistics for this year’s batch. More than half the students with backlogs somehow got placed in mass recruitments because of the lower cutoff criteria this time, while I got locked out of eligibility by 0.1 CGPA. I spent my weekends assisting professors and maintaining a clean record, and now those who skipped classes are getting onboarding dates while I'm facing unemployment. It’s like the system actively rewards mediocrity and punishes actual discipline.

My school friend just posted his 45 LPA placement offer on LinkedIn and I'm sitting here in my damp room, failing to compile a basic AVL tree code for my DSA lab tomorrow. We literally had the same marks in 10th grade, but he got into a tier-1 college because his parents could afford premium coaching. I feel this physical ache in my chest seeing his post, like I've been robbed of a life I was supposed to have, and now I'm stuck with a 3.5 LPA mass recruiter future.

Everyone in my batch walks around with iPads taking neat color-coded notes, ordering Starbucks during lectures, and planning weekend trips to the hills. I'm literally skipping breakfast to save money for my semester exam fees and borrowing old books from the library. It's so unfair that while they get to focus 100% on their GPA, I have to spend three hours daily managing a cheap mess coupon and feeling like a second-class citizen in my own classroom.

My dad spent the entire dinner talking about Sharma uncle's son buying a new Honda City and sending money home to renovate their house. I sat there staring at my plate, suffocating, because I still have two backlogs in math and haven't even cleared the first round of campus placements. Why does it feel like some people are handed the perfect roadmap to success while I'm clawing through mud just to keep my head above water?

I stayed up until 3 AM for three months straight writing that research paper, but the professor gave the prestigious foreign internship recommendation to a classmate whose dad is a department head. It's sickening to realize that no matter how hard I study or how many hours of sleep I sacrifice, my effort is worth nothing compared to someone else's birthright. I just want to throw my laptop away and sleep forever.

We had a group discussion in our MBA class today and everyone was casually throwing around terms like 'synergy', 'leverage', and talking about their summer gigs at McKinsey. I sat in the corner sweating, clutching my cheap plastic folder, praying the professor wouldn't call on me. They have this unearned confidence because they grew up in rich, English-speaking homes, while I have to translate every sentence in my head before speaking and feel like an absolute fraud.

My roommate just landed a 24 LPA placement at an investment bank, and I’m sitting here with three backlogs, struggling to compile a simple graph traversal algorithm in my DSA lab. We used to study together, eat the same cheap maggi, and now I feel this sick, hollow ache in my chest every time he talks to his parents on the phone about signing bonuses while I'm calculating if my 6.2 CGPA will even let me sit for mass recruiters. I don't hate him, but looking at him makes me feel like I’m decaying in real-time.

Everyone in my WhatsApp batch group is sharing screenshots of their summer internship offer letters, and I didn't even make it past the first round of resume shortlisting. I spent my whole semester sacrificing sleep, building projects, and for what? My parents keep asking me why the neighbor's son got into a FAANG company while I’m still begging local startups for unpaid roles. I feel like my life is a resource-allocation bug where I put in maximum input and get absolutely zero output compared to everyone around me.

I saw my high school friend's Instagram story showing off his new apartment in Bangalore and his company-sponsored Macbook. Here I am in my damp hostel room, staring at a screen that’s thermal throttling, trying to debug a Django backend for a college project that nobody will ever care about. We had the exact same board marks, but he got a lucky break with an off-campus referral, and now our lives are on completely different trajectories. It feels like the universe arbitrarily decided to give him a head start while I'm stuck running on a broken treadmill.

My dad called today just to let me know that my cousin got a 12 LPA package straight out of his tier-3 college, and then he asked me how my prep for the service-based company coding test was going. I couldn't even tell him that I got rejected in the aptitude round itself because the shame is literally choking me. It feels like all the resources my family spent on my coaching and tuition are a complete waste, and I'm just a defective investment compared to everyone else in our family tree.

We got our mid-term papers back for Operating Systems, and the class average was 18/25. I got a 12. The guy sitting next to me, who literally plays Valorant all night and skips every lecture, got a 22 and was casually laughing about how easy the grading curve was. I’ve been sitting in the library until 10 PM every single day, taking meticulous notes, and I still failed to even reach the average. It feels like no matter how much effort I pour into this degree, others will always get more reward with zero effort, and I’m just fundamentally stupid.

I can't even look at LinkedIn or our WhatsApp placement group anymore. Everyone is posting about getting 18 LPA, 24 LPA SDE roles at product companies, and here I am, after grinding LeetCode for two years, holding a miserable 4 LPA offer from a mass recruiter. My dad looked at me today and just sighed, saying my cousin already cleared the Google round. It makes me feel like all my late nights in the library were a complete waste of life. Why do they get to fly while I'm stuck in the mud when we did the exact same labs?

Relative grading is an absolute scam. I spent three weeks straight preparing for the Operating Systems midterm, barely slept, and got an 82 which got curved down to a C because the class average was ridiculously high. Meanwhile, my roommate literally copied the entire lab assignment last minute, did zero self-study, and pulled an A- because his viva examiner was chill. It feels so unfair it makes me physically sick. What is the point of actually trying to learn when the system rewards luck and punishes honest effort?

My batchmates at the coaching center are all buying these premium mock test series and taking personal mentoring sessions like it's nothing, while my family had to take a loan just to pay my basic tuition here. They talk about their weekend plans and iPads for note-taking, and I'm sitting here stretching a single notebook, constantly worried if my dad will get another notice for the pending term fee. I feel so small and angry. Why do they get a head start in life just because of their parents' bank accounts while I'm playing on hard mode?

Everyone in my batch is posting their convocation pictures and sharing their 'moving to Bangalore' updates on Instagram, and I'm sitting alone in my hostel room prepping for my third-semester backlog exam. I was always the smart kid in school, and now I'm being left behind to repeat labs with juniors who don't even know my name. It feels like my entire life has been paused while everyone else got to move on to the next level of adulthood. I just feel so empty and deprived of a normal college ending.

I stayed up for three nights straight fixing the bugs in our team's web app for the hackathon, but the team lead gave the presentation credit to his close friend who barely contributed a line of CSS. Now that friend is getting references from the faculty sponsor for summer internships, and I'm left with absolutely nothing to show for my sleepless nights. I feel so cheated and invisible. Why do some people get to climb so easily on other people's backs while I get pushed into the background?

I can't even look at LinkedIn anymore. My lab partner who literally copied my DBMS assignments just bagged a 24 LPA SDE role at an MNC, and here I am, still getting rejected in the resume screening rounds for 6 LPA startups. I've spent nights grinding LeetCode, maintaining an 8.9 CGPA, and for what? It feels like the universe is just mocking my hard work. My dad keeps asking why I didn't get shortlisted for the same company, and I don't even have an answer that doesn't make me sound like a bitter loser.

Why did I even choose Mechanical? My hostel wingmates in CS are already planning their post-grad trips because they got PPOs, while I’m sitting here studying thermal engineering for 14 hours a day just to maybe get a core job that pays peanuts. We put in the exact same amount of sweat, sometimes I even pull more all-nighters, but their baseline starting salary is triple mine. It makes me feel so stupid and left behind, like I ruined my life at 18 by choosing the wrong branch.

Every Sunday call with my parents is just a status report on how my cousin is doing at his IIT. He gets custom tech stacks, funded research trips, and my mom keeps saying 'look at how much exposure he is getting, why are you just sitting in your hostel room?' I didn't choose to go to a tier-3 college because I was lazy; my exam day was a disaster and I panicked. Seeing him get every resource on a silver platter while I have to beg professors here for a basic recommendation letter is eating me alive.

I have to skip the weekend cafe outings with my project group because my monthly budget is literally gone on hostel rent and exam fees. They all casually order 400 rupee coffees and talk about their upcoming Goa trips while I’m calculating if I can afford eggs this week. I work part-time as a content writer after my classes, but I’m still scraping the bottom of the barrel while they get to focus entirely on their resumes. I feel so bitter and isolated from my own friends.

I’m sitting in the library watching everyone around me fill out their onboarding forms for summer internships. I have two active backlogs in math, and because of that, the placement cell won't even let me register on the portal. I feel like a second-class citizen in my own batch. We all took the same admission test, we all sat in the same classrooms, but now they are 'professionals' and I’m just a failure who can't even clear a basic semester exam.

I’ve been grinding LeetCode for 8 months straight, barely sleeping, skipped my sister's wedding prep just to clear the OA. And then my roommate, who literally copied my DBMS assignments all semester, lands an on-campus internship at Microsoft because he lucked out with an easy interviewer. My dad called today asking why I didn't get shortlisted when 'even the slacker in your room got in'. I feel so incredibly hollow. It's like no matter how much sweat I put in, the universe just hands my dreams to everyone else while I get left with backlogs of stress.

Our college shifted to relative grading this semester and it has ruined my mental health. I got an 8.2 CGPA, which used to be decent, but because the average in my batch is insane, my rank plummeted. My friends are putting up their '9.5+ club' screenshots on LinkedIn and celebrating on WhatsApp, and I’m literally sitting here holding back tears because my 8.2 feels like a complete failure now. I worked just as hard as them, but on this curved scale, my hard work was devalued just to make them look better.

Everyone on my college group chat is posting about clearing the first rounds of Goldman and Amazon, talking about 25 LPA packages. I got a 6 LPA offer at a mass recruiter, which I know is better than nothing, but I feel so ashamed to even tell my parents. They sacrificed so much to pay my tuition fees, and now my relatives are already asking which 'dream company' I cracked. I feel so poor and inadequate compared to my peers, like I’m starting life ten steps behind everyone else.

I look at the guys in my project group with their high-end MacBooks, iPad Pro notes, and expensive coaching subscriptions, and then there’s me struggling to code on a laggy 4GB RAM laptop that overheats if I run Docker. We are sitting in the same classroom, but we live in completely different worlds. They talk about weekend trips and expensive cafes so casually while I’m calculating if I can afford dinner after paying my mess dues. I just feel so deprived and angry that my starting line is so much harder than theirs.

I'm from a Tier-3 college and I've built three full-stack projects, contributed to open source, and have a solid portfolio. But when I apply off-campus, my resume doesn't even get past the ATS, while my cousin at a Tier-1 college gets direct interview invites for the same roles just because of his college tag. It makes me want to scream. I’ve worked three times harder than him, but because of an exam I messed up at 18, I'm treated like a second-class citizen in tech. How is this fair?

My roommate just got a 45 LPA offer at a US-based fintech firm while I'm still grinding Leetcode and struggling to clear the initial OA for companies paying 6 LPA. We literally studied the same materials, shared notes, and attended the same shitty lectures. Now he's looking at apartments in Bangalore and I'm calculating how much of my father's retirement fund went into my fees. It feels like we started the race at the same line, but somehow he got a supercar and I was given broken slippers. I don't hate him, but every time he orders Starbucks or talks about his joining bonus, something inside me just withers.

Everyone in my batch has these expensive iPads for note-taking, premium subscriptions to coding platforms, and personal mentors their parents paid for. I'm sitting here in the library using a cracked Android phone to download pirated PDFs of textbook chapters because my family is already struggling with my college loan. During the group project discussion today, they were talking about system design courses they bought online like it was nothing. I feel so starved of basic resources; how am I even supposed to compete on the same grading curve when we are playing on completely different difficulty levels?

My cousin who barely cleared his boards just got placed in a tech sales role making 12 LPA through his dad's connections. I spent my entire college life maintaining a 9.2 CGPA, sacrificed my sleep, got zero social life, and my best offer is an on-campus mass recruiter role for 4 LPA. At dinner tonight, my dad was just quiet, but my uncle called to ask if I wanted him to talk to his contacts to 'help me out.' I felt this sick, burning humiliation in my chest. It's so unfair that years of actual grind mean less than a single phone call from a wealthy relative.

My school friend who was always worse than me in math got into a Tier-1 college because of a lucky day on the JEE advanced, and now his Instagram is just him posting about hackathons, cool campus fests, and getting pre-placement offers from major MNCs. Meanwhile, I'm stuck at this local private college where the placement cell doesn't even bring in core companies, and we're forced to write mindless physical lab manuals in 2024. I feel like my entire career was sabotaged by one bad exam day while he gets to live the dream life I worked ten times harder for.

I had to take a semester back due to a severe case of clinical depression and physical burnout, and now I'm watching my junior batch sit for the internships I was supposed to target. My original batchmates are already posting 'happy to share' updates on LinkedIn about their summer internships at top banks. I'm struggling just to wake up, complete one DSA question, and not cry during my counseling sessions. I feel so utterly left behind, like everyone got to move on with their lives while I got frozen in time, losing my youth and my potential.

I don't even know why I try anymore. My roommate spent his entire third year gaming, barely knew how to reverse a linked list, and just bagged a 28 LPA offer at an MNC because of some internal referral and luck in the interview. Meanwhile, I've solved over 450 LeetCode problems, maintained an 8.9 CGPA, skipped family weddings to study, and all I have is a 6 LPA service-based offer that my dad won't even talk about. It feels like the universe just hoards rewards for the people who don't even care, while leaving some of us to starve on scraps.

My college's WhatsApp group is just a constant stream of bragging. Everyone in my project group got these high-end coaching subscriptions and premium prep materials paid for by their parents, so they easily breezed through the OS and DBMS midterms. I’m out here working a 4-hour night shift at a local store just to cover my hostel mess fees, arriving at exams on 3 hours of sleep, only to get a 6.2 on the relative grading curve. They have all the safety nets in the world and still act like they 'earned' their 9.5 CGPA, while I'm drowning just to stay average.

I had to skip the entire Day 0 and Day 1 campus placement drives because my mother was hospitalized with chronic kidney failure, and I was the only one who could stay by her side. Now, all my batchmates are posting their 'Happily accepted' LinkedIn updates at Amazon and Adobe, while I'm stuck with backlogs of college labs and trying to find off-campus drives that don't even reply. It feels like I paid the price for being a good son, and the reward is watching my career die before it even starts while everyone else gets their dream life.

I feel so pathetic in the coding labs. My laptop is an old 4GB RAM i3 that freezes every time I try to run a Docker container or train a basic ML model for our project, and my group partners get annoyed because my runs take forever. They sit there with their MacBooks and high-end rigs, laughing about compiling errors, while I’m literally sweating, praying my system won’t crash before the final evaluation submission. It’s not just about the tech; it feels like they’re living in a completely different world where progress is instant, and I’m stuck in the mud trying to dig my way out.

I've been working on this ed-tech app idea for over a year, coding late nights after my routine assignments, but had to pause because I can't afford the server hosting fees or API costs anymore. Then this guy in my branch, whose dad owns three factories, copies a basic wrapper template, gets his family to fund a 10 Lakh seed round, and now our college incubator is parading him around like some prodigy. I feel this toxic, burning resentment in my chest because I know my architecture was better, but his privilege bought him the success I literally bled for.

I spent the entire weekend debugging my DSA assignment, barely slept, and still got a TLE on the final test cases. Meanwhile, my wingmate—who literally parties every night and has a rich dad with connections—just casually announced he bagged an on-campus internship at an MNC because his uncle knows the HR. I'm sitting here with a CGPA of 8.4, starving myself to save on mess bills, and it feels like no matter how hard I grind, the game was rigged from the start. Why do some people get a head start in life while I have to kill myself just to reach the starting line?

Just got off the phone with my mom. She was crying because my cousin just got a 24 LPA package at a fintech firm, and she started asking why my preparation isn't matching up. She doesn't get that my college doesn't even get those companies on campus, and I'm struggling with backlogs while working part-time to pay my tuition fees. My cousin had a private tutor and his own room, while I share a tiny, noisy hostel room with three other guys and study under a single desk lamp. I feel so hollow inside—it’s like I was born with a deficit I can never outrun.

Everyone in the class group is sharing their winter internship offer letters, and I'm just sitting here staring at my empty inbox. I worked through every single coding contest, maintained a 9.1 CGPA, and didn't even get a single interview shortlist because of some stupid legacy hiring policy. These guys who copied my lab code are getting placed left and right just because they have better soft skills and polished LinkedIn profiles. I feel like an absolute ghost, watching everyone else move on with their lives while I’m stuck in this endless loop of rejection.

I had to skip the department trip because I couldn't afford the registration fee, and today my feed is flooded with photos of my classmates enjoying at the resort. They're all talking about it in the coding lab, laughing about inside jokes, while I'm pretending to be hyper-focused on my system design project so I don't cry. They don't have to worry about student loans or sending money back home; they get to just 'experience college life.' I hate how much I resent them, but I can't help feeling like I'm being punished for a life I didn't choose.

My lab partner got a fully funded research internship in Europe because his professor is his dad's childhood friend. I’ve written to fifty professors, customized every single cold email, read countless research papers, and all I got was automated rejections. He didn't even know what the project was about until last week, and now he's posting visa updates on his story. I feel so small and utterly defeated; what is the point of working hard when nepotism and luck decide everything anyway?

My roommate got a 24 LPA offer at a fintech firm during day 0 of placements. He literally slept through half the DBMS lectures while I was grinding LeetCode till 3 AM everyday. I ended up with a 6 LPA service-based role and my dad spent yesterday's phone call asking why I couldn't crack the same round when we share the exact same room and books. I feel so hollow and sick to my stomach, like all my effort was just a joke.

I got an 8.2 CGPA this semester, which is honestly my best yet, but everyone on the class WhatsApp group is complaining about getting 'only' 9.1 or 9.4. My parents saw the group chat and asked why I'm celebrating mediocrity when others are crying over near-perfect scores. It feels like no matter how much I climb, the ground beneath me just sinks further because of how easily everyone else seems to fly.

I'm sitting here in my 10x10 PG room looking at my backlog list, while my school friend who didn't even qualify for JEE is posting stories from a private college in Pune, driving a car, and talking about his 'hustle'. My family took a massive loan for my coaching, and I’m surviving on instant noodles just to fail my supply exams. Why do some people get a head start in life without even trying, while my entire existence is just a struggle to stay at zero?

We had our system design project evaluations today and my group partner got a paid remote internship offer directly from the external examiner because of 'good networking'. I did 80% of the actual coding, wrote the entire documentation, and stayed up debugging while he just gave a slick presentation. I’m stuck looking for unpaid work to satisfy our curriculum requirements while he's already earning; it feels so unfair it physically hurts.

My batchmates from college are posting LinkedIn updates about getting promoted to SDE-2 or moving to Europe for their MS, and here I am still trying to clear my remaining three papers while working a dead-end tech support job. I used to be the school topper, but now when I see their achievements, I just close my eyes and feel this suffocating dread. Why did everyone else get the manual on how to succeed while I got left behind in the mud?

My roommate just bagged a 25 LPA package at an MNC during the day-1 placements. We literally prepped DSA together, solved the same LeetCode problems, and stayed up until 4 AM drinking cheap coffee. Now he's buying a new iPhone and talking about shifting to a luxury PG, while I'm sitting here with zero offers, three rejects, and an empty bank account. I don't hate him, but it physically hurts to look at him. Why does it feel like I worked just as hard but got left in the dirt?

Everyone in my class is posting their summer internship certificates on LinkedIn, talking about 'learning and growing' at tech startups. My parents sacrificed their savings so I could come to this private college, but because of my 6.8 CGPA, I couldn't even clear the resume cutoffs. I spent my whole summer doing free content writing for a local shop just to have something on my CV. I feel so cheap and left behind when I see them talking about their stipends and office perks. Did my parents waste their money on me?

My cousin and I joined the same coaching institute for JEE prep. He got into a tier-1 IIT and is now going to weekend treks and coding fests, posting cool stories with his rich friends. I ended up in a local tier-3 college with broken labs and professors who don't even show up. My relatives keep calling my dad to ask when I'm getting 'placed' like him. I've been grinding 12 hours a day on web dev, but it feels useless because the companies don't even visit our campus. Why did one exam decide that he gets a premium life while I have to beg for a 3 LPA service-based job?

I had to skip the college department trip because my family is currently going through a financial crisis after my dad's business took a hit. Now my WhatsApp group is flooded with photos of my classmates clubbing, eating gourmet food, and renting luxury villas. I'm sitting in my hot room, eating instant noodles, trying to debug a stupid React app for a freelance gig that pays pennies. I feel this sickening knot in my stomach. Why does everyone else get to enjoy their youth while I have to work like a 40-year-old just to pay my exam fees?

My lab partner got his research paper accepted in an IEEE journal. The funny thing is, I did 70% of the actual coding and data cleanup because he kept slacking off, but his uncle is the department head, so his name went first. Now he's getting congratulated by all the faculty, and he's probably going to get a direct recommendation for MS in the US. I got a tiny mention in the acknowledgments. I feel completely cheated and invisible. How do I sit next to him in lab tomorrow without losing my mind?

Everyone in my wing is celebrating. My roommate just got placed at a fintech giant with a 24 LPA package, and he literally copied my DSA codes during the lab exams. I'm here sitting with my 7.2 CGPA, skip-counting meals to save money, wondering why my dad has to take another loan just for my semester fees while this guy gets a signing bonus that could clear my family's entire debt. I don't begrudge him, but it hurts so bad to feel this left behind when I worked twice as hard.

My cousin who didn't even study half as much as me got into a tier-1 college because his parents could afford the premium coaching classes and personal tutors. I had to self-study from pirated YouTube videos while managing my mom's clinic runs. Now at family gatherings, my uncle keeps bragging about his kid's future 'global exposure' while my parents just look down at their plates in silence. I feel so bitter and hollow inside; it's like my effort never even stood a chance against their money.

I spent the entire semester in the library, barely sleeping, just to clear my math backlog. My lab partner literally partied every weekend, barely opened the textbook, and somehow cleared it with an A grade because his uncle is on the department board. I got a bare pass grade. It makes me want to scream because the system is so rigged, and I'm exhausting myself to death just to get crumbs of what others get handed on a silver platter.

I look at girls in my hostel wing who wake up at 5 AM, hit the gym, attend all lectures, run three clubs, and still secure 9.5 CGPA. I have chronic fatigue and ADHD, and just waking up and attending one coding lab feels like climbing Everest. I feel so cheated by my own brain and body. Why do I have to fight a war inside my head just to survive a basic Tuesday, while they get to live life on easy mode?

Every time I open LinkedIn, it's a stab to my chest. My school batchmates who went to IITs are posting about their international internships at Google and Meta. Meanwhile, I'm stuck in a tier-3 college where mass recruiters haven't even visited yet, coding on a laggy 4GB RAM laptop that overheats if I run two Docker containers. I worked just as hard as them in school, but one exam day went wrong, and now I'm condemned to a completely different, lower-class life. I feel so empty and cheated by fate.

My roommate just got placed at a fintech firm with a 24 LPA package. I've been grinding Leetcode till 3 AM every day, and I can't even clear the OA for basic service companies. We literally started coding at the same time, used the same resources, but he gets everything while I'm stuck worrying if I can even pay off my student loan. It feels like the universe just decided I don't deserve a good life, no matter how hard I work.

Just saw the GPAs posted on the department board. My cousin, who literally spends all day gaming, got a 9.4 CGPA because his prof is super chill with grading. I got a 7.1 because my evaluator is notorious for failing people, even though I didn't sleep for three days straight before midterms. My parents are already calling me, asking why I can't be more like him. It makes me want to throw up; my effort literally means nothing here.

I hate looking at LinkedIn and Instagram. All my high school friends who went to Tier-1 colleges are posting about their massive tech internships and foreign exchange programs. Meanwhile, I'm stuck in this Tier-3 college where companies don't even visit for placements, and we have mandatory 75% attendance for useless lectures. I feel like I was locked out of a good future the day I messed up my JEE mains.

We had a group discussion today for our final project, and everyone was talking about buying expensive online bootcamps and iPads for note-taking like it's pocket change. I'm literally skipping meals to afford my hostel fees and practicing coding on a laggy, second-hand laptop that crashes every time I run a heavy Docker container. I'm working twice as hard just to stay at the baseline where they start from. It's so unfair it physically hurts.

My lab partner is already contributing to open source and solving Hard problems on Leetcode like it's nothing. I'm still struggling to write a basic binary search without looking up the syntax, and the professor keeps pairing us up. Every time we do a coding run, I just sit there feeling like a total fraud, waiting for him to realize how dumb I am compared to him. Why does it come so naturally to everyone else while I have to bleed for every single line of code?

My lab partner literally copied my DSA assignments the whole semester and somehow just got a 25 LPA package at a product company, while I'm still struggling to get shortlisted for mass recruiters. My dad called me today asking why I didn't get the same placement when we studied together. I feel sick to my stomach. I did all the actual coding, but he gets the life-changing offer while I am staring at rejection emails.

Everyone in my hostel wing is celebrating right now. This guy who literally slept through all our core OS classes just got an internship through some internal reference, while I've been grinding LeetCode day and night with a 9.1 CGPA and got absolutely nothing. It feels so unfair, like the universe is mocking my effort. I am locked in my room crying because I don't want them to see me like this.

My cousin who dropped out of college is earning lakhs a month through some dropshipping business, and my parents won't stop bringing it up at dinner every single night. Here I am, burning my eyes out studying 14 hours a day for GATE, sacrificing my physical health, only to be treated like an unproductive burden. I feel so deprived of simple respect in my own home just because my timeline looks different.

Our class WhatsApp group keeps buzzing with 'Extremely happy to share that I've joined...' updates, and I am sitting in my dark room with three backlogs in systems programming. We all started from the exact same coaching center in high school, but they got the good packages, the relationships, and the perfect college life while I got stuck in this depression loop. Why did I get left behind so badly?

It hurts so much seeing my wealthy batchmates get easy project evaluations because their families are connected to the professors, while my external examiner ripped my database project apart despite all the genuine research I did. Why do some people get the smooth, paved highway while I have to bleed for every single mark? I feel completely powerless and empty.

My roommate just bagged a 32 LPA offer at Atlassian. I was the one who taught him basic recursion and graph algorithms during our DSA lab last semester. Meanwhile, I got rejected in the first round of a mass recruiter paying 4 LPA because of my 7.2 CGPA. I spent my entire summer coding while he was gaming, and now his parents are sending sweets to my house while my dad is looking at me like I'm a massive financial burden. Why does it feel like the universe took my hard work and handed it to someone else?

Everyone in my batch is posting about their summer internships on LinkedIn. My WhatsApp group is filled with congratulations stickers for people who literally copied assignments from GitHub. I'm sitting here with two active backlogs, trying to figure out how to pay this semester's tuition fees because my dad's shop took a hit. I don't even hate them, I just feel this deep, crushing hollow in my chest. Why do they get a smooth runway while I have to fight for basic survival?

Just had my project evaluation. The professor didn't even look at my backend architecture—just saw a tiny UI alignment bug and gave me a C. Meanwhile, the group next to us copy-pasted a template from YouTube, put on a fake accent, and got an A+. I stayed up for three nights straight subsisting on chai and maggi, and for what? It feels so unfair that honest effort is actively punished here while superficial showoffs get the spoils.

My cousin just got his MS admit from a top US university, and my mom has been on call with my aunt for two hours. Now she's dropped the 'look at him, and look at you sitting in a local college with zero placements' bomb. I didn't choose to go to a Tier-3 college; we couldn't afford the coaching fees for JEE back then. I study 12 hours a day for GATE, but to my family, I'm just the cheap failure who didn't make the cut. I feel so starved of just a little bit of pride from them.

I see my college friends posting stories from weekend trips to Goa and showing off their new mechanical keyboards bought from their stipend money. I had to skip lunch yesterday because my monthly allowance ran out early and I didn't want to stress my parents. I've worked so hard on my development skills, but because our college doesn't get on-campus drives, I'm stuck. It's like I'm standing behind a glass window watching everyone else live the actual college life while I'm just rotting in my room.

My roommate barely spent two hours on Leetcode, spent the entire semester partying, and got a 45 LPA domestic offer because his cousin works as an EM there. I've spent every single night since third year grinding DSA, making projects, and I can't even get a shortlist for a 6 LPA service company. It makes me feel so sick to my stomach. Why did I sacrifice sleep, health, and everything just to watch someone else cruise into a secure life without trying?

Everyone in my lab has M3 Macbooks that compile high-scale ML models in seconds. I'm stuck with a refurbished 8GB ThinkPad that freezes every time I run a Docker container. I failed my mid-semester lab evaluation because my local environment crashed twice during the live run while the guy next to me got full marks in ten minutes. It’s so exhausting starting every single day with this massive handicap and knowing my grades are taking a hit just because I can't afford better hardware.

My dad took a personal loan to send me to this college, and I'm surviving on a strict budget. Yesterday, my cousin got placed at a tier-1 product company with a 30 LPA package, and my relatives immediately called my dad to rub it in. He didn't say anything to me, but I could hear the disappointment in his voice when he asked about my low CGPA. Why do some people get effortless brains, rich parents, and perfect luck, while my family has to bleed just to get me a degree that might not even land me a basic TCS job?

I have to manage all the groceries, cook for my sick mother, and handle local freelance gigs just to pay our rent, all while keeping up with college. Meanwhile, my classmates spend 12 hours a day in the library or doing high-profile, unpaid research internships that build their resumes. I had to skip the placement prep mock tests today because I was at the hospital. I feel so bitter watching them discuss their career trajectories when I'm just trying to make sure we don't get evicted next month.

I got a backlog in Discrete Math last semester because I was recovering from typhoid, and now I'm blocked from applying to any company with a 'no active backlogs' policy. My friends are all posting their group photos from their pre-placement dinner parties on WhatsApp. I’m sitting in my dark room, studying for the makeup exam, feeling like a complete failure. It's so unfair that one bad month wiped out all my hard work while they get to celebrate their clean slates.

Everyone in my wing got placed during day 0. Even guys who used to copy my DBMS lab codes got 24 LPA packages, and here I am, still sitting with a 6.5 CGPA and zero offers. My parents called to ask why our neighbor's son got into a FAANG company while I can't even clear the first round of a mass recruiter. It's not just that I don't have a job, it's that I worked twice as hard as them throughout college, skipped every fest to study, and ended up with absolutely nothing while they coasted through. I feel so bitter and hollow inside.

I saw the WhatsApp group updates of my school friends buying cars and moving to Bangalore for high-paying SDE roles. I had to drop out of my coaching institute because we couldn't afford the loan interest anymore, and now I'm stuck preparing for state exams at home in a single room. It's so unfair. We all started at the same desk in school, but their dad's money bought them elite college packages, and my family's financial crisis has completely derailed my life. I feel trapped and so angry at my situation.

My roommate got a research internship in Germany through a cold email, and I got rejected from even the local college projects. We both applied with the same resume format, but his family had connections with the department head. I've spent the last three days staring at my wall, unable to code or even go to the mess for dinner. It feels like no matter how much I optimize my LeetCode runs or practice system design, the deck is already stacked against me. Why do some people get everything handed to them while others have to beg for crumbs?

It's semester results day and I'm sitting in the washroom crying because I got a 7.2 GP while the rest of my study group cleared 9+. They are all planning a trip to celebrate, and I'm here calculating if I'll even clear the CGPA cutoff for the upcoming campus placements. I was the topper in my school, but here, I feel like the dumbest person in every room. Why is my best effort not even close to their average?

My cousin who didn't even study for the board exams got into a private college through management quota and already has a pre-placement offer of 18 LPA because of his uncle's business network. Meanwhile, I cracked JEE with a decent rank, spent four years burning my eyes out over DSA sheets, and now I'm facing a recession with zero callbacks. I feel so much resentment when my parents compare our progress during family calls. It makes me want to delete my LinkedIn and block everyone I know.
